messages.subject: Differences between 'replicate' and group with 'iid'
parts:
Dear INLA community,

Hi, I am wondering the differences between 'replicate' feature and grouping with 'iid'.
As far as I understand, they both seems like having a shared prior (hyperparameters or population-level parameters) with iid individual-level estimates.

So, what's the difference between 'replicate' and grouping with 'iid'?

Thanks in advance for your helpful comments!
Minho

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Differences between 'replicate' and group with 'iid'
parts:
replicate is the same as group with iid.

is was just handy, for coding reasons, to allow replicate within the
group framework.


> y = rnorm(10)
> r = g = 1:10
> i = 1
> r1 = inla(y~-1+f(i,model="iid", replicate = r), data =
data.frame(y,i,r)); r1$mlik
[,1]
log marginal-likelihood (integration) -18.87122627
log marginal-likelihood (Gaussian) -19.33785642
> r2 = inla(y~-1+f(i,model="iid", group =
r,control.group=list(model="iid")), data = data.frame(y,i,r)); r2$mlik
[,1]
log marginal-likelihood (integration) -18.87122570
log marginal-likelihood (Gaussian) -19.33785597
> r3 = inla(y~-1+f(r,model="iid"), data = data.frame(y,i,r)); r3$mlik
[,1]
log marginal-likelihood (integration) -18.87122570
log marginal-likelihood (Gaussian) -19.33785597

>
